_comment: Assistant safety settings for Windows (the worker settings of settings.example.windows.json with the assistant mode: an assistant is a persistent session that reads the project and changes nothing in it; macOS / Linux: settings.example.assistant.json). Replace C:/ABSOLUTE/PATH with the absolute path of the project's core copy, <project>/coordinator/core (the folder that holds scripts/), written with FORWARD slashes: Claude Code runs hook commands through Git Bash on Windows, which drops backslashes, and a hook that fails to run blocks nothing (start-worker refuses a backslash there). This is the SWARM and STANDARD baseline (CORE section 3): only the protected branches and irreversible removals are guarded; workers do routine risky work themselves and report it. The STRICT preset adds "Bash(gh pr merge*)", "Bash(gh pr ready*)" and the production MCP write tools; the CAUTIOUS override also adds "Read(**/.env*)" and the stack candidates chosen in the init quiz (TOOLKIT.md Safety). Also add gh pr merge / ready denies wherever PROJECT.md says humans merge or mark ready. MCP tools bypass the hook (it sees only the shell and edit tools), so their writes are denied here: the names assume the GitHub MCP server is connected as "github" (mcp__<server>__<tool>) - rename them to the server name this machine uses, and add the write tools of any other connected server that can change a protected branch. Drop mcp__github__merge_pull_request only where workers merge their own PRs (PROJECT.md). attribution hides the AI co-author trailer, the PR line and the session link: artifacts are in the owner's voice (CORE section 11). env COORD_PROTECTED_ROOT is the project's working copy (the owner's checkout, the project root): replace C:/ABSOLUTE/PROJECT with its absolute path; the guard then refuses Edit / Write / MultiEdit / NotebookEdit under it outside its .claude/worktrees/ (hence those tools in the PreToolUse matcher). env COORD_PROTECTED_BRANCHES names the branches the guard protects besides main and master, which it always protects (empty here: main and master only): names separated by spaces or commas, each matched whole and literally (no patterns), letter case ignored - a list adds to main and master, never replaces them; the push deny rules below name main and master only - a project listing more branches adds the same deny rules for each of them (TOOLKIT.md Safety). SendMessage is in the matcher too: the guard refuses a message to a session of another project, as it refuses claude stop / rm / respawn / attach / --resume of one (CORE section 1.17). env COORD_ASSISTANT_DIR is the assistant's own folder: replace C:/ABSOLUTE/PROJECT/coordinator/assistants/NAME with its absolute path (NAME: the assistant's name); with it set, the guard holds the session to an assistant (#281): Edit / Write / MultiEdit / NotebookEdit only inside that folder (also inside COORD_PROTECTED_ROOT, whose worker rule then gives way), any other path refused; git only to read (log, show, diff, status, branch listing, fetch ...: commit, push, merge, checkout, stash, add and every other write refused, in any repository); gh only a known read, an allowlist (pr / issue / repo / run ... list, view, status, diff, checks, watch; search, status, auth status, gh --version, help; gh api with no method and no fields, or -X GET; graphql without a mutation): every other gh command refused (an alias and its call, an extension, auth login, config set, an unknown group ...). A value that is not absolute refuses every edit. Shell file writes (redirection, sed -i ...) are not guarded: the assistant's brief holds it to its folder there. Which connectors an assistant may use is its brief's, from the owner. The compact hook runs after-compact.ps1 assistant: after each compaction the assistant re-reads its own BRIEF.md and NOTES.md (COORD_ASSISTANT_DIR) and the core's roles/assistant.md, never a worker's kept brief, which it outlives. This file only - never the coordinator's own settings, which edit there (TOOLKIT.md Safety).
